subject: Renewal discussion: commit flexibility, grace period, and per-token ceiling
participants_external: sam.taylor@acme.com (Sam Taylor, Head of AI Product, Acme AI)
messages:
From: Sam Taylor <sam.taylor@acme.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: 2027-03-21T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal: commit bands & flexibility for next period

Marcus —

Thanks for the Q1 usage report (attached) and for the initial renewal deck. We ran the numbers and expect a seasonal dip over the next two quarters driven by a temporary deprioritization of one product line. That means we need to talk about:

- Right-sizing our committed tokens for the upcoming 12-month term (looking to reduce ~$200k in commit)
- A 1–3 month grace period where we can underdeliver against the commit without heavy penalties
- Rollover of unused committed tokens (or credit) for at least one quarter rather than immediate forfeiture
- A hard per-token ceiling on overage pricing (we can’t accept unconstrained step ups at renewal)

The simplest path for us would be either a) shrink the commit and accept a slightly higher per-token overage, or b) keep the commit but introduce a short grace/rollover window so we don’t lose credit from the dip.

Can you share specific options and the economics so we can take to procurement? I’ve attached our Q1 usage export. Procurement wants a concrete option they can sign off on.

Thanks,
Sam
Sam Taylor
Head of AI Product — Acme AI
Attachments: ACME_usage_report_Q1.xlsx

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Sam Taylor <sam.taylor@acme.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2027-03-21T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: commit bands & flexibility for next period

Sam —

Appreciate the context and the usage export. Two pragmatic options we typically propose for customers in this situation (summary below — attaching a clean terms snapshot):

Option A — Flexible banding (lower commit, tiered per-token):
- Reduce annual commit by ~20% (saves ~200k in commit)
- Per-token overage tiers with a mild step-up after 120% of monthly pacing
- No rollover; smaller overage discount at lower volumes
- Target: minimal contract churn, predictable unit economics

Option B — Fixed commit (no change) + first-quarter rollover credit + short grace window:
- Keep the current commit level for 12 months; allow up to 15% of unused committed tokens to roll forward into Q1 of the new term (one-quarter roll forward)
- Provide a 30-day grace window at the start of the term before overage rates apply
- Slightly better per-token pricing vs Option A (because commit remains)

Quick notes on per-token ceiling: we can lock a per-token ceiling for the first 6 months of the new term (example: $0.0035/token ceiling for overage) to protect you against sharp step-ups. Any permanent ceiling beyond 6 months would require an uplift to the annual commit price.

Next steps: if you prefer Option B, we’ll produce a redlined term sheet (DocuSign-ready) and route to procurement. If you prefer Option A, we’ll model the final numbers and include a sample monthly pacing schedule so procurement can see the variance. 

I’m attaching a quick terms snapshot (redwood_proposed_terms_v1.pdf). For internal logistics: lauren, rishi — can you confirm how long a rollover-credit window we’re comfortable offering and whether we should cap it at 15% or 12%? If procurement wants PO-first, we’ll include that in the execution path.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0183
Attachments: redwood_proposed_terms_v1.pdf

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2027-03-21T11:10:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Renewal: commit bands & flexibility for next period — recommended negotiation plan

Lauren / Rishi —

Forwarding Sam’s note. Quick recommendation for negotiation posture: 

- Priority = preserve ARR while avoiding a cliff for the customer. Offer rollover or short grace in exchange for either a modest uplift in committed ARR or a one-time non-refundable credit.
- Rollover window: target 1 quarter (we can go to 3 months) but cap roll forward credits at 12% of annual commit to protect economics.
- Grace period: 30 days is low friction and gives them runway; 60 days pushes economics a bit too far unless we get a commensurate price uplift.
- Per-token ceiling: offer a 6-month fixed overage ceiling (e.g., $0.0035) as a concession. If they want a permanent price ceiling, we need a larger commit or a small uplift to the committed $/token baseline.
- Sales motion: get procurement to sign PO for the commit and use DocuSign for the term amendment. Legal redlines low-risk — standard rollover language.

Ask: can you run a quick sensitivity on ARR delta for a 12% vs 15% rollover cap and share which is acceptable for quota/forecast? I’ll position Option B (keeps commit + small rollover) as our preferred path in the next email.

Thanks —
Marcus

Marcus —

Thanks for the fast response and the two options. Procurement reviewed internally and here’s where we landed:

- We prefer Option B (keep commit + rollover/ grace) — it preserves budget cadence for us and keeps the relationship stable.
- Request: can you make the rollover cap 12% (instead of 15%) and confirm the 30-day grace window? That hits our internal controls for forecast accuracy.
- We also need a 6-month overage ceiling guaranteed in writing (as you suggested) — please put that in the term sheet.
- Next step: please send a redlined term amendment we can attach to the PO. Procurement will issue a PO once the amendment reflects the 12% cap and includes a signature block.

If you can get the DocuSign link over today, I’ll loop in procurement and legal on our side.

Appreciate it —
Sam
